html:
SMTO-EXE-0252 — SMTO couldn't find steps in this task that it can reuse

GUID: 25060c31-766e-5958-a5f6-8ffa3816253a
Slug: recipe-capture-no-reusable-steps
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • SMTO tried to turn this finished task into a step-by-step workflow, but couldn't confirm which steps could be safely repeated. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find your original message in the conversation and select Save to workflow. This saves your exact request and settings, without needing to copy each step the task took.
  2. In the dialog, review the request and settings, then select Save workflow. The saved workflow then appears on the Workflows page, ready to start with Run now.
  3. If the task was very long, split the job into smaller requests and save each one as its own workflow. Step-by-step recording only works for tasks of limited length.

What success looks like

  • The workflow appears on the Workflows page, and Run now starts a new task from it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the original task just to make a workflow; it may repeat changes it already made.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Workflow capture could not build a reusable step graph from the run: results, declared outputs or dependencies were missing, a step ran in the background, the run used parameter bindings, or it exceeded the capture limits.

What this means

  • Capture could not prove a bounded reusable graph: receipts, declared outputs, dependency closure, supported foreground effects or required selected steps were missing or exceeded capture limits. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • Capture could not prove a bounded reusable graph: receipts, declared outputs, dependency closure, supported foreground effects or required selected steps were missing or exceeded capture limits.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect capture eligibility and structured receipt/dependency coverage, including the 512-row bound, without reconstructing steps from transcript prose.

How to fix it

  • Check the rejection in src/agent_runtime/recipes/recorder.py (extract, visit, convert, capture): capture needs successful structured results with declared result fields, dependencies in source order, no background or terminal_detached steps, no parameter bindings, at most 512 operations and 64 selected steps, and every write included. Save the request as a saved-request workflow instead.
  • Review why capture is unavailable and record a supported bounded run with verified structured receipts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported bounded run produces a saveable capture with all required effects represented.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
